summary: Water quality monitoring in Chile has historically been a challenge due to the low density of measurement stations, with only 829 stations covering more than 12,000 lakes and 1,200 rivers. Traditional methods, based on sporadic in situ sampling, did not allow for continuous monitoring or early detection of problems such as eutrophication or pollution. To address this limitation, we developed an advanced monitoring system using remote sensing technology. Through satellite images, hyperspectral spectroscopy and bio-optical models, we were able to assess and monitor water quality in four strategic lakes in south-central Chile: Laguna Grande de San Pedro de la Paz, Lago Lanalhue, Lago Villarrica and Lago Llanquihue.

summary: The project aims to develop a high-throughput phenotyping system for Eucalyptus spp. by integrating 3D and hyperspectral data, supplemented by artificial intelligence tools. The goal is to identify, based on the plants’ spectral signatures and structural characteristics, areas affected by abiotic stress and to generate indicators that enable early and accurate detection of stress.

summary: Automatic characterization of river morphology provides valuable information for understanding river dynamics and supporting management and restoration. This study aimed to semi-automatically characterize the River Styles of the Duqueco River in south-central Chile using the South Rivers Toolbox (SRT), a QGIS tool developed to extract hydromorphological metrics and classify river segments. A total of 43 River Styles were identified, showing distinct characteristics along the upper, middle, and lower reaches. The results demonstrate that SRT can support the retrospective analysis of river evolution and identify sections sensitive to geomorphological changes, providing useful information for assessing flood risk and river management.
